evidence.quote: third quarter revenue was $412.3 million, up 14% from $361.7 million in the prior-year quarter
Annual recurring revenue from our Fernhill Orchestrate software platform reached $588 million at quarter end, up 22% from a year ago
Gross margin expanded to 47.8%, compared with 46.1% a year ago
Adjusted operating margin was 15.2%, up from 13.9% in the third quarter of last year
Adjusted earnings per share were $0.74, compared with $0.61 a year ago
Free cash flow was $38.5 million in the quarter
We booked $445 million of new orders in the quarter, which translates into a book-to-bill ratio of 1.08
our backlog closed the quarter at a record $1.21 billion
Net revenue retention on software was 118% in the quarter
we are raising our fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $1.62 billion to $1.66 billion, up from our prior range of $1.58 billion to $1.63 billion
We continue to expect an adjusted operating margin of approximately 15% for the full year
We are lowering our fiscal 2026 free cash flow guidance to $120 million to $135 million, compared with our previous range of $140 million to $155 million
For the fourth quarter, we expect revenue in the range of $435 million to $450 million

tone.label: constructive
tone.justification: Management reported a record quarter above its own range and raised full-year revenue guidance, which supports a positive label. It was also explicit about weaker European orders and the cash cost of tariffs, and it declined to discuss fiscal 2027 margins, so the tone is constructive rather than confident.

evidence.quote: The third quarter was our strongest quarter to date
decision cycles are clearly longer, and we are planning conservatively for the region
we are not going to give fiscal 2027 guidance today

risks.title: Slower European orders
risks.description: European grocery and apparel customers are delaying investment decisions; orders fell 9% and the revenue impact lags by two to three quarters.

evidence.quote: European orders were down 9% year over year

risks.title: Tariffs on imported components
risks.description: New tariffs on motion-control components raise costs; management expects to offset most of it only by mid next year.

evidence.quote: New tariffs on imported motion-control components took effect in August

risks.title: Pre-bought inventory ties up cash
risks.description: Securing component supply required an inventory build, which is the main reason free cash flow guidance was cut.

evidence.quote: We have secured supply for the next two quarters, but we pre-bought inventory to do so — and that ties up cash.

risks.title: Competitors pricing aggressively on smaller projects
risks.description: Fernhill is not matching lower prices, which may cost some deals near term.

evidence.quote: We are seeing some competitors become more aggressive on price for smaller projects

risks.title: Customer concentration
risks.description: The largest customer is 17% of revenue year to date; the renewal reduces but does not remove the risk.

evidence.quote: We do still regard customer concentration as a risk

analyst_questions.question_summary: Why cut free cash flow guidance by about $20 million while raising revenue, and is it really timing?
analyst_questions.answer_summary: About $15 million is pre-bought inventory and about $5 million absorbed tariff cost; the inventory is tied to backlog projects shipping in the first half of fiscal 2027.

question_evidence.quote: You are raising revenue but cutting free cash flow by about $20 million at the midpoint

answer_evidence.quote: about $15 million is the component inventory we pre-bought and about $5 million is tariff cost we have absorbed

analyst_questions.question_summary: Does the raised revenue range assume price increases to offset tariffs?
analyst_questions.answer_summary: Only already-announced increases on new orders since September; the benefit builds mainly in fiscal 2027.

question_evidence.quote: does the raised revenue range assume any price increases to offset the tariffs?

answer_evidence.quote: It includes the price increases we have already announced, which took effect on new orders from September

analyst_questions.question_summary: Is the European slowdown a pause or a shift away from automation, and what is assumed for Q4?
analyst_questions.answer_summary: Described as a delay, not a shift; Q4 assumes European orders stay at Q3 levels; management would not call the bottom.

question_evidence.quote: Is this a temporary pause, or are you seeing customers shift budgets away from automation altogether?

answer_evidence.quote: What we hear from customers is that projects are still on their roadmaps, but boards are asking for more certainty

analyst_questions.question_summary: Should investors expect pricing pressure and lower margins next year?
analyst_questions.answer_summary: Management declined to give fiscal 2027 guidance before January and pointed to software mix and its margin framework.

question_evidence.quote: should we expect pricing pressure and a step back in margins next year?

answer_evidence.quote: we are not going to give fiscal 2027 guidance today; we will do that in January as usual

analyst_questions.question_summary: Is the multi-year renewal with the largest customer on track?
analyst_questions.answer_summary: Signed in October as a five-year agreement; the customer was 17% of revenue year to date.

question_evidence.quote: is the multi-year contract renewal still on track for this year?

answer_evidence.quote: I am pleased to say we signed the renewal in October

analyst_questions.question_summary: What is the price uplift from Orchestrate 5 upgrades and when does it reach ARR?
analyst_questions.answer_summary: Around 25% subscription uplift for customers taking both modules, flowing into ARR at renewal dates over four to six quarters.

question_evidence.quote: How should we think about the price uplift per customer, and when does that show up in annual recurring revenue?

answer_evidence.quote: the upgrade carries an average subscription uplift of around 25% for customers who take both new modules
